free_tier.stated: these pay you; they do not sell to you. Honeygain 10 GB = $1 ($0.10/GB); PacketStream $0.10/GB; EarnApp moved to hourly pay on 20 Aug 2025, ceiling $10/IP/month in the US and $5 elsewhere; Pawns.app, Repocket and Traffmonetizer publish no rate; Grass pays in points with no dollar rate

egress.terms: N/A - no HTTP egress endpoint is sold to consumers by any of them

record.interface_detail: none exposed to a buyer at consumer tier
record.chaining: none - but this tier is the source of the bytes that PacketStream/Proxyrack resell, which is why their retail floor is $1/GB
record.limits_note: Residential bandwidth sharing applications do not expose HTTP proxy egress endpoints directly. Software clients sell device bandwidth wholesale to residential proxy aggregators (such as Bright Data, IPRoyal, and PacketStream). Contributors receive fixed cash payouts per gigabyte rather than reciprocal routing credits.
record.reliability_note: Per-IP caps and per-IP demand make earnings non-scalable; Honeygain's own example needs three separate networks to reach $5-6.67/month; Emerging Threats now ships 'ADWARE_PUP: Bandwidth Sharing Tool' rules for 5 of these 8 domains, so IDS-equipped networks flag them.

evidence.proved: 'Only 2 of the 8 apps publish what they pay per gigabyte, and both pay $0.10'; 'A gigabyte that earns you $0.10 sells for a median $4.50, a 45x markup'; 'EarnApp ... pays at most $10 a month per US IP address ... Outside the US the ceiling is $5'; 'Pawns.app, Repocket and Traffmonetizer don't publish a rate, and Grass pays in points'
'Network-contribution programs like Grass reward uptime consistency instead: no per-GB meter, no per-minute tally'; per-unit apps 'typically between 20 cents and $1 per gigabyte'
'$2 starting gift'; rates not restated on the homepage
Emerging Threats rules table: PacketStream, EarnApp, Pawns.app, Traffmonetizer, Repocket, Grass each get 2 rules in category ADWARE_PUP added 11 Feb 2026
